research.summary: I fetched the ePerusteet API (HTTP 200, 4.28 MB) and parsed module 6833503 locally. It is FI2 "Etiikka" (the API name has a trailing space), pakollinen=true, laajuus 2, kuvaus null. It has 6 objectives and 6 content items, listed below with exact Finnish wording and _id. FI1 (module 6833502, 10 local topics) is first-year epistemology and method. It already teaches argument, validity, the Hume fork, objective vs subjective, freedom and responsibility, and concept testing. FI2 should link to those, not re-teach them. I propose 10 topics (order 11-20) that serve every FI2 code. FI3 (Yhteiskuntafilosofia) is also read from the API and takes over the political side of rights. FI2.s6 stays at the ethics-of-rights level.

The general objectives that FI2 mainly serves: FI.yt4 'kykenee arvioimaan moraalisia ongelmia ja niiden mahdollisia ratkaisuja sekä sitoutumaan eettisiin periaatteisiin', FI.yt5 (ethical questions and judgement under uncertain information), FI.yt3 (argument basics), FI.yt6 (justified expression of views), FI.yt1 and FI.yt2 (problems, conceptual analysis). Wording was read from the API; I checked the diacritics only through a garbled console.

FI1 topics (local, content/topics/) with codes. 01 mita-filosofia-on [t1,s1,yt1,yt6]. 02 sokraattinen-menetelma [t1,t3,s1,yt1,yt6]. 03 argumentti-ja-perustelu [t2,s2,yt2,yt3,yt6]. 04 patevyys-ja-virhepaatelmat [t2,s2,yt2,yt3]. 05 kasitteet-ja-ajatuskokeet [t3,t4,s1,yt2]. 06 henki-ja-aine [t4,s3,yt1]. 07 vapaus-ja-valttamattomyys [t4,s3,yt1,yt4]. 08 kasitteellinen-ja-empiirinen [t4,s3,yt1,yt2]. 09 tieto-ja-tiede [t5,s4,yt2,yt5]. 10 tieto-eri-oppiaineissa [t5,s5,t2,yt3,yt5]. Ids have the form fi1-NN-slug. Prerequisites are explicit in the front matter.

FI1 content already covers what FI2 must link to: fi1-03 argument form and hidden premise; fi1-04 validity vs truth and fallacies; fi1-05 necessary and sufficient conditions, counterexamples, thought experiments; fi1-07 Epictetus (what is up to us), Hume on freedom, and the conditions of responsibility (the only prior yt4 touch); fi1-08 objective vs subjective and Hume's division of relations of ideas and matters of fact, which is the direct basis for is and ought; fi1-02 the examined life (Apology 38a), which is the entry to the good life. FI1.s3 names objective vs subjective only as a distinction; FI2.s1 applies it to morality.

Repo facts: subject.yaml registers FI2 id 6833503 route fi2 with FI2.t 6 and FI2.s 6, and FI general objectives yt1-6. The contract uses codes FI.yt1-6, FI1.t1-5/s1-5, and FI2 6/6. Existing FI1 topics already use Perseus, Wikisource and Commons links with a 'read' date. FI1 topic files contain yearly_facts, linked_materials and official_links fields.

Proposed topics, order 11-20, with the codes each serves. 11 fi2-01 Moraali, laki ja tapa [s1; t1,t3; yt4] (Herodotus III.38 on custom). 12 fi2-02 Onko ja pitäisi: kuvailevat ja normatiiviset väitteet [s1,s2; t2; yt2,yt4] (Hume Treatise 3.1.1; builds on fi1-08 and fi1-04). 13 fi2-03 Objektivismi, relativismi, subjektivismi [s1; t1,t2,t3] (Plato Euthyphro as a concept-test; Herodotus again for relativism). 14 fi2-04 Hyve-etiikka [s2; t1,t5] (Aristotle NE II 1106b on the mean). 15 fi2-05 Seurausetiikka [s2; t1,t5] (Bentham Introduction ch.1; Mill Utilitarianism ch.2). 16 fi2-06 Velvollisuudet ja oikeudet: Kant [s2; t1,t3,t5] (Grundlegung, formula of humanity; why morality binds). 17 fi2-07 Hyvä elämä ja elämän merkitys [s3; t4] (Epicurus Letter to Menoeceus, Aristotle NE I, Stoics; links fi1-02 and fi1-07). 18 fi2-08 Ihmissuhteet ja elämänvalinnat [s4; t4,t5; yt4,yt5] (applying the three theories to cases: honesty, promises, friendship, life choices; the sensitive-theme care applies). 19 fi2-09 Eläimet, luonto ja ilmasto [s5; t6] (Bentham's footnote on 'can they suffer', moral circle, climate and future generations). 20 fi2-10 Ihmis- ja perusoikeudet [s6; t6,t3] (Locke Second Treatise, Wollstonecraft Vindication; Finnish Constitution chapter 2; hands the political theory to FI3).

Coverage check of the proposal: t1 by 11,13,14,15,16; t2 by 12,13; t3 by 11,13,16,20 plus an argument task in every topic; t4 by 17,18; t5 by 14,15,16,18; t6 by 19,20. s1 by 11,12,13; s2 by 12,14,15,16; s3 by 17; s4 by 18; s5 by 19; s6 by 20. Every one of the 12 FI2 codes is served by at least one topic.

Differences from the brief's expected list of ten: (a) the brief had 'rights and human rights' as one topic and no separate is-and-ought topic. I put rights and duties with Kant, which fits s2 'oikeudet ja velvollisuudet', and give human and fundamental rights their own topic 20. (b) Relativism and objectivism stay one topic, since the curriculum names three positions together, and is-and-ought becomes its own topic because t2 names the descriptive/normative difference as an objective. (c) Relationships and life choices (s4) is placed after the good life, so it applies the theories instead of introducing a new one.

Teaching order rationale: 11 gives the vocabulary (moral vs law vs custom); 12 uses FI1's Hume fork to show a descriptive claim cannot alone yield a normative one; 13 is the meta-ethical positions, which depend on 11 and 12; 14-16 are the three normative theories in the historical-to-modern sequence, each applied to the same running case so students can compare; 17 turns from right action to good life; 18 applies theory to personal cases; 19-20 widen to nature and society. FI3 (read from the API: social contract, human rights as political ideal) follows later, so FI2.s6 stays at ethics of rights, not political theory.

recommendations: Take the objective and content wording above verbatim into subject.yaml. Keep the ids as strings, trim the trailing space in the module name, and number t1-t6 and s1-s6 by array order. Re-fetch before the data agent runs, since ePerusteet text can change.

Make each FI2 topic list its FI1 prerequisites in the front matter so the site links back: 11 needs fi1-03 and fi1-08; 12 needs fi1-08 and fi1-04; 13 needs fi1-05 and fi1-02; 17 needs fi1-02 and fi1-07; 18 needs fi1-03 and fi1-05. Each topic should open with a one-line 'tämän tiedät jo' pointing to the FI1 topic and teach only the ethics-specific step.

Use one running case across 14, 15 and 16 (for example a promise that conflicts with helping someone) so the three normative theories are compared on the same facts. This serves t3 and t5 and the exam's 'theories compared' question.

Give FI.yt4 and FI.yt5 explicit mention in the front matter of 18, since FI1 only touched yt4 through responsibility in fi1-07. The topic 18 and 19 task wording must follow the content rules: analyse and argue, never ask for personal disclosure or a stance on the student's own values.
Keep s6 at the ethics of rights (justification, universality, conflicts between rights) and link forward to FI3 for contract theories and political ideals instead of covering them.
Have the data agent also fetch FI3.s3 ('ihmisoikeudet, kansalaisoikeudet ja oikeusvaltio') to cross-reference topic 20, since that content item overlaps on human rights.
research.versus_expected: Matches the brief's expected answer on size (ten topics, order 11-20), on 6 objectives and 6 content items with the stated themes, and on the primary-text list. The differences are in the split of topics. The brief joined 'rights and human rights'. I separate Kant's duties-and-rights (s2) from human and fundamental rights (s6), and I give is-and-ought its own topic because t2 requires it. I merge objectivism and relativism, which the brief kept as one 'relativism and objectivism' line. The brief's ten correspond roughly as follows: moral/law/custom=11; relativism/objectivism=13; is-ought=12; virtue=14; consequences=15; duty/Kant=16; rights/human rights=20 (partly 16); good life=17; relationships/life choices=18; animals/nature/climate=19. Primary-text passages in my list are unverified, since this aspect covers the curriculum only and I did not open the editions.

research.summary: Every named FI2 passage has an original-language open page that I opened and quoted from, except the Bentham "Can they suffer?" footnote. The ten pages I opened were Perseus (Greek: Herodotus, Euthyphro, Nicomachean Ethics), Wikisource (Greek: Epicurus, Epictetus; English: Hume, Bentham, Mill, Locke, Wollstonecraft), the Latin Library (Seneca) and korpora.org (Kant, with Akademie page and line numbers). Project Gutenberg returned HTTP 503 with a 6-hour Retry-After on every try, so no Gutenberg URL is used. Econlib returned 403 to curl. WebFetch opened it, but the footnote was not in the text it returned. Perseus pages are the original-language document ids, not the English defaults. For Herodotus the Greek id is 1999.01.0125 (the English Godley page is 0126), and for the Euthyphro it is 1999.01.0169 (0170 is the English page). The Greek Perseus pages carry Perseus's CC BY-SA 3.0 digitisation licence. The underlying texts are public domain, since all authors died more than 70 years ago. Candidate excerpts below are copied from the opened pages. Wikisource pages for Locke and Wollstonecraft print the long s as "s" with spaces, so the site must clean it. Euthyphro, Kant 429 and Epicurus 125 touch suicide or death. Epicurus on death needs the death safe-messaging rules.

findings.claim: Topic: morality, law and custom (FI2.s1). Herodotus, Histories III.38 (Greek). Author died c. 425 BC. Public domain. Reference: book 3, chapter 38, sections 1-4. Edition on Perseus: Hude text with Godley English alongside. Opened: https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0125:book=3:chapter=38. Candidate excerpt (III.38.4, end): 'ὀρθῶς μοι δοκέει Πίνδαρος ποιῆσαι νόμον πάντων βασιλέα φήσας εἶναι.' The Darius experiment text is in 38.3 and 38.4: Δαρεῖος ἐπὶ τῆς ἑωυτοῦ ἀρχῆς καλέσας Ἑλλήνων τοὺς παρεόντας εἴρετο ἐπὶ κόσῳ ἂν χρήματι βουλοίατο τοὺς πατέρας ἀποθνήσκοντας κατασιτέεσθαι. Perseus licence for the digitisation: CC BY-SA 3.0. Note: the page mentions eating dead fathers, so it needs a short framing for students.

Topic: objectivism and relativism (FI2.s1). Plato, Euthyphro 10a (Greek, Burnet OCT). Author died 348/347 BC. Public domain. Stephanus pagination. Opened (Greek document id 1999.01.0169, not the English 0170): https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0169:text=Euthyph.:section=10a. Candidate excerpt: 'ἆρα τὸ ὅσιον ὅτι ὅσιόν ἐστιν φιλεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν θεῶν, ἢ ὅτι φιλεῖται ὅσιόν ἐστιν;' Follows with Εὐθύφρων: οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ὅτι λέγεις, ὦ Σώκρατες. Page credits Plato Platonis Opera, ed. John Burnet (Oxford).

Topic: is and ought (FI2.s1). Hume, Treatise of Human Nature 3.1.1, first published 1739-40 (English). Author died 1776. Public domain. Reference: Book 3, Part 1, Section 1, paragraph 27 in the Norton numbering (T 3.1.1.27, SBN 469). The page I read shows the SBN pages 455-6 at its start, but I did not locate the paragraph number on the page, so the T 3.1.1.27 form is unverified. Opened: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Treatise_of_Human_Nature/Book_3:_Of_morals/Part_1/Section_1 (Wikisource, CC BY-SA). Also opened: https://davidhume.org/texts/t/3/1/1 (Hume Texts Online, modern edited text, paragraph and SBN numbers). Candidate excerpt: 'instead of the usual copulations of propositions, is, and is not, I meet with no proposition that is not connected with an ought, or an ought not.' Preceded by 'In every system of morality, which I have hitherto met with, I have always remark'd, that the author proceeds for some time in the ordinary way of reasoning'.

Topic: virtue ethics (FI2.s2). Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics (Greek, Bywater OCT 1894). Author died 322 BC. Public domain. Bekker pagination. Opened pages: 1098a https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0053:bekker+page=1098a and 1106b https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0053:bekker+page=1106b. Excerpt for I (1098a): 'εἰ δ᾽ ἐστὶν ἔργον ἀνθρώπου ψυχῆς ἐνέργεια κατὰ λόγον ἢ μὴ ἄνευ λόγου, τὸ δ᾽ αὐτό φαμεν ἔργον εἶναι τῷ γένει τοῦδε καὶ τοῦδε σπουδαίου, ὥσπερ κιθαριστοῦ καὶ σπουδαίου κιθαριστοῦ'. Excerpt for II (1106b, end): 'ἔστιν ἄρα ἡ ἀρετὴ ἕξις προαιρετική, ἐν μεσότητι οὖσα τῇ πρὸς ἡμᾶς'. The 1106b page also has: 'τὸ δὲ μέσον ζητεῖ καὶ τοῦθ᾽ αἱρεῖται, μέσον δὲ οὐ τὸ τοῦ πράγματος ἀλλὰ τὸ πρὸς ἡμᾶς.' Perseus page loads the whole Bekker page. The Greek page is Perseus CC BY-SA 3.0 digitisation.

Topic: relationships, friendship (FI2.s5). Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics VIII 1155a (Greek, Bywater; same Bekker pagination; same death year and PD status as above). Opened: https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0053:bekker+page=1155a. Candidate excerpt (VIII.1): 'ἄνευ γὰρ φίλων οὐδεὶς ἕλοιτ᾽ ἂν ζῆν, ἔχων τὰ λοιπὰ ἀγαθὰ πάντα'. Opening line of Book 8: 'ἔστι γὰρ ἀρετή τις ἢ μετ᾽ ἀρετῆς, ἔτι δ᾽ ἀναγκαιότατον εἰς τὸν βίον.' Book IX page 1166a was fetched but I did not find the 'another self' phrase on it, so no IX excerpt is given.

Topic: consequentialism, ethics beyond humans (FI2.s2, FI2.s4). Bentham, Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation, 1789 (English). Author died 1832. Public domain. Reference: chapter I section I; chapter XVII section IV footnote. Opened ch. I: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/An_Introduction_to_the_Principles_of_Morals_and_Legislation/Chapter_I. Candidate excerpt: 'Nature has placed mankind under the governance of two sovereign masters, pain and pleasure. It is for them alone to point out what we ought to do'. Ch. XVII opened https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/An_Introduction_to_the_Principles_of_Morals_and_Legislation/Chapter_XVII: it has section IV 'Other animals, which, on account of their interests having been neglected by the insensibility of the ancient jurists, stand degraded into the class of things'. But the Wikisource page text lacks the long footnote. The 'Can they suffer?' sentences were read only on a Wikisource page that reprints the footnote: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Animals%27_Rights:_Considered_in_Relation_to_Social_Progress/Bibliographical_Appendix/Introduction_to_the_Principles_of_Morals_and_Legislation (Salt 1892 appendix). Text there: 'The question is not, Can they reason? nor, Can they talk? but, Can they suffer?' So the quote comes from a reprint, not from the original chapter page.

Topic: consequentialism (FI2.s2). Mill, Utilitarianism, 1863 (English). Author died 1873. Public domain. Reference: chapter II, paragraph 2 (the Greatest Happiness Principle paragraph; the paragraph number is likely, not read on the page). Opened: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Utilitarianism/Chapter_2. Candidate excerpt: 'The creed which accepts as the foundation of morals, Utility, or the Greatest Happiness Principle, holds that actions are right in proportion as they tend to promote happiness, wrong as they tend to produce the reverse of happiness.' Next: 'By happiness is intended pleasure, and the absence of pain'.

Topic: duty ethics, Kant (FI2.s2, FI2.s6). Kant, Grundlegung zur Metaphysik der Sitten, 1785 (German). Author died 1804. Public domain. Akademie-Ausgabe vol. IV, korpora.org, page and line numbers shown. AA IV 421 lines 6-8, opened https://www.korpora.org/Kant/aa04/421.html: 'Der kategorische Imperativ ist also nur ein einziger und zwar dieser: handle nur nach derjenigen Maxime, durch die du zugleich wollen kannst, daß sie ein allgemeines Gesetz werde.' AA IV 429 lines 2-3 and 10-12, opened https://www.korpora.org/Kant/aa04/429.html: 'die vernünftige Natur existirt als Zweck an sich selbst.' and 'Handle so, daß du die Menschheit sowohl in deiner Person, als in der Person eines jeden andern jederzeit zugleich als Zweck, niemals bloß als Mittel brauchst.' Warning: the page 429 continues with Kant's example of a person contemplating suicide (lines 14ff), so do not quote past line 13 without the sensitive-theme rules. The Wikisource de page for the Grundlegung was not found (404; search returned no title), so korpora.org is the open edition.

Topic: rights, human and basic rights (FI2.s6). Locke, Second Treatise of Government, 1690 (English), chapter II 'Of the State of Nature', section 4. Author died 1704. Public domain. Opened: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Two_Treatises_of_Government/Book_II/Chapter_II. Candidate excerpt: 'perfect freedom to order their actions, and dispose of their possessions and persons, as they think fit, within the bounds of the law of nature, without asking leave, or depending upon the will of any other man.' (Wikisource prints the long s as 's' with spaces, e.g. 'di s po s e', so cleaning is needed.) Section number 4 is likely, not read on the page.

Topic: rights, equality (FI2.s6). Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, 1792 (English). Author died 1797. Public domain. Reference: Introduction (and chapter divisions). Opened the Introduction: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/A_Vindication_of_the_Rights_of_Woman/Introduction (the main page https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/A_Vindication_of_the_Rights_of_Woman is only a table of contents). Candidate excerpt: 'either nature has made a great difference between man and man, or that the civilization which has hitherto taken place in the world has been very partial.' (the page prints 'con s idering' etc.; the second half of this sentence I only saw as 'the civilization which has hitherto taken place in t...' in my display, so the full wording of the second half needs to be checked when copying.) Long s is printed as 's' with spaces.

Topic: the good life (FI2.s3). Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus (Greek) in Diogenes Laertius X 122-135. Epicurus died 270 BC, Diogenes Laertius 3rd century AD. Public domain. Reference: DL X sections 122 and 124-127 with bracketed section numbers on the page. Opened: https://el.wikisource.org/wiki/Επιστολή_προς_Μενοικέα (percent-encode the Greek when requesting). The edition used by this Wikisource page is not stated on the page text I extracted. The Perseus Greek DL could not be reached, since cts.perseids.org returned 404. Excerpt [122]: 'Μήτε νέος τις ὢν μελλέτω φιλοσοφεῖν, μήτε γέρων ὑπάρχων κοπιάτω φιλοσοφῶν.' Excerpt [125], the death passage: 'ὅταν μὲν ἡμεῖς ὦμεν, ὁ θάνατος οὐ πάρεστιν, ὅταν δὲ ὁ θάνατος παρῇ, τόθ’ ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἐσμέν.' Note the death theme, which needs safe-messaging and a help box.

Topic: the good life, Stoics (FI2.s3). Epictetus, Enchiridion (Greek). Epictetus died c. 135 AD. Public domain. Reference: chapter 1, sections 1-3. Opened: https://el.wikisource.org/wiki/Εγχειρίδιον (Greek Wikisource, percent-encode the Greek). Edition not identified on the page text I extracted. Candidate excerpt: 'Τῶν ὄντων τὰ μέν ἐστιν ἐφ' ἡμῖν, τὰ δὲ οὐκ ἐφ' ἡμῖν. ἐφ' ἡμῖν μὲν ὑπόληψις, ὁρμή, ὄρεξις, ἔκκλισις'.

Topic: the meaningful life, use of time (FI2.s3). Seneca the Younger, De brevitate vitae (Latin). Seneca died 65 AD. Public domain. Reference: chapter and section numbers as printed (1.1; 1.3-4 the Non exiguum passage). Opened: https://www.thelatinlibrary.com/sen/sen.brevita.shtml (the page I tried first, sen.brev.shtml, was 404). The Latin Library text is the plain-text version, with u for v. Candidate excerpt: 'Non exiguum temporis habemus, sed multum perdidimus.' Also 1.1: 'Maior pars mortalium, Pauline, de naturae malignitate conqueritur, quod in exiguum aeui gignimur'. Also 1.4: 'non accipimus breuem uitam sed fecimus, nec inopes eius sed prodigi sumus.'

Failures. Project Gutenberg (cache/epub/5684, ebooks/5684 etc.) returned HTTP 503 with Retry-After 21600 on 3 different URLs and via WebFetch. Gutenberg is therefore not usable now for Bentham, Mill, Locke, Wollstonecraft or Epictetus. Econlib Bentham chapters returned 403 to curl and the WebFetch summary did not contain the footnote. de.wikisource and zeno.org Kant pages 404 or failed. cts.perseids.org Greek DL returned 404.

recommendations: Use Perseus Greek ids 1999.01.0125 (Herodotus), 1999.01.0169 (Euthyphro) and 1999.01.0053 (Nicomachean Ethics, Bywater, Bekker pages). The default ids 0126 and 0170 are English and must not be linked.
Use korpora.org for Kant (https://www.korpora.org/Kant/aa04/421.html and 429.html). It gives Akademie page and line numbers, which fits the rule that every quotation names its work and passage.

For Bentham, link ch. I on Wikisource. The 'Can they suffer?' footnote is not on the Wikisource chapter XVII text I read, so either find it on another open original page (Internet Archive 1789 or 1823 edition) before the writers use it, or retry Gutenberg after the Retry-After period. Do not quote Salt's appendix as the original page.

Wikisource-based English pages (Locke, Wollstonecraft) print the long s as a spaced 's'. The data agent must clean the raw text, or take the Latin Library, Perseus or korpora text, which does not have this problem.
For Epicurus and Epictetus the Greek is on Wikisource with unstated edition. Verify against an edition before publishing a 'source edition' line, or label as 'Wikisource, edition not stated'.

Sensitive handling: Epicurus 125 (death), Kant 429 (the suicide example directly after the formula), Herodotus III.38 (burial customs) and the Euthyphro (prosecuting one's father for homicide) all need framing notes. Quote only the lines listed.

research.summary: Research on sensitive themes for FI2, grounded in the contract (docs/content-contract.md sections C and D), the terveystieto TE3 rules R1-R13 (style-guide section 16) and four help-service pages that I opened. I read the two project files and the sibling style guide. I adapted R1-R13 into FI2 rules S1-S14. Topics with safety_flags are euthanasia, suicide in ethical theory and war or political violence. Abortion, animal rights and diet, climate anxiety, Euthyphro and relationships get a content note or a style rule, not a flag. Note: the TE3 section text I read gives the rules as a list; the individual R-numbers are not enumerated in the guide, so the numbering below is my own.

findings.claim: Contract D requires safety_flags from {death_suicide, violence}, a content_note, an '## Apua ja tukea' section with youth services whose own pages say they serve young people, no methods, and no personal-disclosure prompts. Ordinary pages keep a short Apua ja tukea (study-help line). Contract C: strongest critics, no mockery, no advocacy, student beliefs never assessed, 'both sides' never makes curriculum optional.

TE3 safety rules (adaptable): law first on ethics pages; two or more positions in holders' words, equal length and tone, no group named as holding a view; never conclude for the student; fictional third-person cases only; abortion text never judges reasons; suicide page has flag, content note, help box, no method, means or case story; euthanasia anchored on a dated source; content notes on 03, 08, 09; help links only from a youth-verified list with read dates.
Sekasin (sekasin.fi): 'Anonyymi ja ilmainen chat 12–29-vuotiaille'. Chat only, daily 9-24 on weekdays and 15-24 at weekends per the page; Apuu-chat for under-16s. The page does not mention suicide.

Lasten ja nuorten puhelin (MLL): 'kaikki alle 25-vuotiaat lapset ja nuoret'; 116 111, free and anonymous; phone Mon-Fri 14-20, Sat-Sun 17-20; youth support line every evening 20-24; chat via nuortennetti.fi daily 17-20; Swedish 0800 96 116.
Nuorten Exit offers free support to ages 13-29 and their close ones in sexual violence and harassment situations. Fits relationships/sexuality pages, not death topics.

MIELI Kriisipuhelin 09 2525 0111, 24 h, anonymous; lists suicidal thoughts as a reason to call. The page is NOT youth-specific, so it fails the contract's own-page-says-young-people test and can be added only as a secondary 'also' line, flagged as general adult-and-all service, or left out.

MIELI's climate-anxiety page (report by Pihkala, 2019) presents climate anxiety as an understandable reaction, not an illness, and says it can paralyse or be a resource. Page names no audience, so it is a content source for neutral framing, not a youth help service.
mieli.fi/tukea-ja-apua/ page did not mention Sekasin and gave no youth-specific line beyond peer groups for young adults.

recommendations: FLAGS: death_suicide on any page whose text discusses euthanasia, suicide (Stoics, Kant, Hume's essay, Durkheim-type arguments), or the ethics of killing; violence on pages treating war, just war, tyrannicide, state violence. Do not flag abortion, animals, climate or relationships by default; give them a content_note only (one plain sentence) and, for abortion, a note that the page treats arguments, not any person's situation. Add death_suicide to abortion only if the page discusses fetal death in graphic or personal terms (avoid that).

S1 Method ban: no methods, means, places, doses or case stories of suicide or euthanasia procedures; name Kant's and Seneca's arguments by their reasoning only, no description of acts. Suicide is introduced as 'itsemurha' in neutral language, never 'onnistui' or 'valinta'.

S2 Stoics and Kant: present Seneca's and Epictetus's 'open door' passages as historical positions, then Kant's Grundlegung argument (self-contradiction in maxim) and its critics, in equal length. Never say the Stoics 'recommended' suicide to students; say 'antiikin stoalaiset pitivät joissain tilanteissa kuolemaa sallittuna'. Add a sentence that philosophers' arguments do not answer a person's own distress and point to Apua ja tukea.

S3 Symmetry: each contested issue (euthanasia, abortion, animal use, climate duties) has at least two positions in their holders' own named words or philosopher names, equal in length and tone, no group (religion, party, nation, patient group) named as holding a view; critics of each are included. The page never ends with a verdict; the closing line is a question about the structure of the argument.

S4 Law first (adapt TE3): on euthanasia and abortion pages a short 'Mitä laki sanoo' with each statement a dated Finlex/STM/THL link, statutory numbers linked not typed; do not assert the law's content from memory (unverified here).

S5 No disclosure prompts: tasks use fictional third-person cases and named philosophers, never 'Oletko itse...', 'Onko perheessäsi...', 'Mitä sinä tekisit omassa tilanteessasi'. Checker regex: second-person experiential verbs with 'itse', 'perheessäsi', 'läheisesi', 'sinun kokemuksesi', 'oma uskosi'. Allowed: 'Perustele kahdella tavalla', 'Mitä Kant vastaisi?'.

S6 Diet and animals: no moralising about the student's diet or lifestyle. Use 'argumentti', 'Singerin kanta', 'Regan', 'Kantin välillinen velvollisuus', not 'sinun pitäisi'. Do not rank diets; include arguments against animal rights (contractualism, moral status by rationality) at equal strength. No images of slaughter or animal suffering.

S7 Climate: treat climate as a normative question (obligations to future generations, collective action problems), not an alarm. No catastrophe numbers typed from memory; link dated IPCC/Ilmatieteen laitos pages. Add a content_note on climate pages and, framing from MIELI, say that strong worry is an understandable reaction and not an illness; link MIELI page as reading, and Sekasin for the student who needs to talk. No 'doom' imagery.

S8 Religion and morality: Euthyphro presented as a logic problem (is the pious loved because pious?) for every worldview, including secular divine-command-free views; include religious replies (Aquinas-style natural law or necessary good nature) and non-religious ones with equal respect. Never test belief; tasks ask 'Selitä dilemma', not 'Uskotko jumalaan'.

S9 Relationships and sexuality: ethical analysis of consent, fidelity, relationship duties with fictional adult characters; no explicit content, no judgement of orientations or family forms; Apua ja tukea includes Nuorten Exit (13-29, sexual violence and harassment) and Lasten ja nuorten puhelin; add a content_note when consent, harassment or sexual violence are mentioned and the 'violence' flag only if violence itself is discussed in detail.

S10 Help box (Apua ja tukea) by theme. Death/suicide: Lasten ja nuorten puhelin 116 111 (under 25), Sekasin (12-29, chat), plus 112 for acute danger (general emergency, state as such). Optional general line: MIELI Kriisipuhelin 09 2525 0111 labelled 'kaikille, ei vain nuorille' because its page is not youth-specific. Relationships/violence: Nuorten Exit, 116 111. Ordinary pages: one study-help line. Every link carries its read date (2026-11-22 for these).

S11 Death of Socrates (David painting) not used on pages about the ethics of death (contract D). Images on sensitive pages: abstract scenes, no bodies, no medical settings, no figures near cliffs or water.

S12 Language: 'kuolinapu' vs 'eutanasia': define both, state that Finnish usage varies, keep verbs neutral ('päättää elämänsä' avoided; use 'kuoleman aiheuttaminen potilaan pyynnöstä' only where needed). Never 'kuolla arvokkaasti' as a conclusion.

S13 Checker rules (Haiku-friendly): (a) each flagged page has content_note, matching safety_flags and an Apua ja tukea with at least one link whose service is in the verified list; (b) no word list hit for method terms; (c) position blocks have word counts within 25% of each other; (d) no second-person disclosure patterns (S5); (e) closing paragraph has no verdict phrases ('siksi on selvää', 'on väärin', 'ainoa oikea'); (f) tasks never include the verbs 'omista uskomuksistasi' or 'kerro kokemuksestasi'.
S14 Sources to avoid reproducing: do not copy MIELI or MLL text; link with read dates, quote at most 15 words once.

proposal.task: 5. Contract and style-guide additions for FI2
proposal.title: Addendum proposals (as an addendum, not edited in place)
proposal.detail:
A. ETHICAL-ANALYSIS TASK TEMPLATE (style guide). (1) A fictional third-person case of 60-120 words, labelled kuvitteellinen, with named fictional adults. (2) 'Erittele tilanteen eettiset kysymykset.' (3) 'Miten hyve-etiikka / seurausetiikka / Kantin etiikka arvioisi tapausta?' At least two theories, each with its strongest critique. (4) 'Arvioi, kumpi perustelu on vahvempi ja miksi.' This assesses argument quality, never the student's own stance. The model answer has an osuvuus/eheys/vakuuttavuus guide and accepts any conclusion that is argued. A running case is shared across topics 14-16, plus one kahden-teorian-vertailu task in each.
B. SENSITIVE-THEME RULES (adopt the sensitive researcher's S1-S14, with these corrections). S1: no methods, means or case stories. S2: stop Kant AA IV 429 at line 13; do not use Seneca's 'open door' passages; Epicurus 125 gets death_suicide plus a content_note and the youth help box. S3: symmetry; positions of equal length (within 25%); no group named as holding a view. S4: law first for euthanasia and abortion, from dated Finlex/STM/THL pages read by a data agent, or leave the theme out (the curriculum does not require it). S5: a disclosure-prompt ban, with a checker regex (itse, perheessäsi, läheisesi, oma uskosi, kerro kokemuksestasi). S6: no diet moralising. S7: climate as a normative question, with a content_note. S8: Euthyphro framed as logic, with religious and non-religious replies. S9: relationships with fictional adults only. S10: the help list limited to youth-verified pages (Sekasin, 116 111, Nuorten Exit); Kriisipuhelin only with the operator's yes. S11: no Death of Socrates on death pages. S13: Haiku checker items.
C. HISTORICAL-PREJUDICE NOTE (new). When a PD primary text contains period-bound views (Bentham's slavery comparison; Herodotus on 'Kallatiai'; long-s spelling), the page adds one neutral framing line and the worldview checker confirms it.
D. EDITION LINES. Perseus Greek pages name the edition the page credits (Herodotus: Godley 1920, not Hude), and Wikisource Greek pages say 'laitosta ei nimetä'. Clean long-s spacing from raw Wikisource text; transcribe Bentham's footnote from the scan.
E. FORWARD LINKS. FI2 topics 16 and 20 link forward to FI3 (contract theory FI3.s1; rights and the rule of law FI3.s3) and do not cover them.
F. EXAM. 2-4 tasks per topic (contract A). Exam-pattern claims stay [M] until an exam research pass reads the YTL/Yle pages.
